newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha shrugs off weaker crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha shrugs off weaker crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha shrugged off a sharp fall in overnight crude prices and fell only moderately on Wednesday, supported by better market sentiment, traders said.
"It's not like regional fundamentals have strengthened much, but more traders are now likely to see the market turning firmer after last week's losing streak," one trader said.

Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was assessed at $208.00/209.00 per tonne, compared with $210.00/211.00 in late dealing on Tuesday. It was rumoured to have been traded at $208.00 early Tuesday trading.
The one-month spread from first-half July was discussed at a backwardation of 50 cents/$1.00, after being traded at a backwardation of 50 cents on Tuesday.

In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, a European trader was said to have sold 900,000 barrels of Indonesian cargoes to the United States. The price was unavailable, but it was linked to West Texas Intermediate on NYMEX, traders said.

Petrochemical firm Showa Denko said it will probably shut one of the two naphtha crackers at its Oita plant in western Japan for two weeks in May due to technical problems. The cracker has ethylene output capacity of 220,000 tonnes a year.
